n.1: The FCA Board oversees conduct regulation, not prudential objectives.
n.2: The Treasury Committee scrutinises regulators, but does not oversee statutory objectives directly.
n.3: The CMA enforces competition law, not prudential regulation.
n.4: Courts hear legal appeals, not oversee prudential regulation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive harmonises conduct standards for investment firms?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: MiFID II harmonises conduct standards across EU investment firms, ensuring transparency and investor protection.

n.1: Solvency II governs insurers, not investment firm conduct.
n.2: UCITS regulates funds, not investment firms.
n.3: PSD regulates payment services, not investment firms.
n.4: BRRD covers bank recovery, not conduct standards.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive requires banks to maintain recovery and resolution plans?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive requires banks to prepare recovery and resolution plans to manage potential failures.

n.1: MiFID II regulates securities markets, not resolution planning.
n.2: Solvency II applies to insurers, not banks.
n.3: UCITS covers investment funds, not bank resolution.
n.4: PSD covers payments, not bank resolution.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: When must the FCA consult on changes to Listing Rules?
o: After HM Treasury approval is granted
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: Under its rule-making powers, the FCA generally consults before significant Listing Rule changes.

n.1: Treasury approval is not a prerequisite for FCA consultation, which precedes rule changes.
n.2: Consultation is not limited to emergencies, since routine rule changes require consultation.
n.3: Consultation is event-driven, not tied to an annual schedule.
n.4: Consultations are initiated by the FCA’s proposals, not individual firm requests.

n.1: The Basel Committee develops bank capital standards but the FSB monitors G-SIBs.
n.2: IOSCO focuses on securities regulation, not G-SIBs.
n.3: The IMF promotes stability but does not designate G-SIBs.
n.4: The World Bank funds development, not systemic bank oversight.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which statement about Section 166 FSMA (skilled person) is accurate in the UK framework?
o: Both FCA and PRA may require a skilled person review
Only the FCA may commission a skilled person report
Only the PRA may commission a skilled person report
It applies solely to listed issuers on the Main Market
It replaces on-site supervisory visits for all dual-regulated firms
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: Section 166 empowers both regulators—the FCA and the PRA—to appoint or require a firm to appoint a skilled person to report on specified matters to assist supervision.

n.1: The power is shared by both regulators, not only the FCA.
n.2: The PRA also uses s.166 where appropriate; it is not exclusive to one regulator.
n.3: The power is not confined to listed issuers; it applies to authorised firms in scope.
n.4: Skilled person reviews complement, rather than universally replace, supervisory visits.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which global body issues principles for effective securities regulation?
o: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: IOSCO develops international principles for securities regulators to promote fair, efficient, and resilient markets.

n.1: The Basel Committee focuses on banks, not securities.
n.2: The FSB coordinates across sectors but IOSCO sets securities principles.
n.3: The IMF monitors global stability, not securities regulation.
n.4: The OECD promotes economic policy, not securities principles.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the FSCS’s relationship with the PRA and FCA?
o: FSCS is accountable to both regulators
FSCS directly regulates banks and insurers
FSCS sets capital requirements for firms
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Services Compensation Scheme is accountable to both the PRA and FCA, providing consumer protection through compensation arrangements.

n.1: The FSCS does not regulate firms directly; it compensates eligible claimants.
n.2: Capital requirements are set by the PRA, not FSCS.
n.3: Monetary policy decisions are made by the MPC, not FSCS.
n.4: Authorisation is handled by PRA or FCA, not FSCS.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive requires disclosure for packaged retail investment products?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The PRIIPs Regulation requires standardised disclosure documents to help retail investors compare packaged products.

n.1: MiFID II governs conduct, not PRIIPs disclosure forms.
n.2: UCITS governs collective funds but PRIIPs applies more broadly.
n.3: Solvency II applies to insurers, not PRIIPs disclosure.
n.4: PSD2 covers payment services, not investment disclosures.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which role does HM Treasury play in relation to financial regulation?
o: Sets the statutory framework for regulators
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: HM Treasury sets the statutory and policy framework under which the regulators operate, providing strategic direction and accountability structures.

n.1: Supervising firm conduct is the FCA’s role.
n.2: Capital requirements are set by the PRA, not Treasury.
n.3: Authorisation decisions sit with FCA or PRA, not Treasury.
n.4: Listing rules are administered by the FCA, not Treasury.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: When is HM Treasury most likely to issue strategic recommendations to the FCA?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: HM Treasury issues recommendations around strategic priorities, particularly when objectives are updated by legislation.

n.1: An enforcement case is operational FCA business, whereas Treasury recommendations address strategic priorities.
n.2: A capital breach is a prudential supervision issue, while Treasury recommendations concern broader strategy.
n.3: Interest rate decisions are for the MPC, not a trigger for Treasury recommendations to the FCA.
n.4: IPO timetables are market operations, not the context for Treasury strategic recommendations.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the FCA’s role in relation to market abuse?
o: Investigate and enforce against market abuse
Set monetary policy to reduce market abuse
Provide emergency liquidity for market abuse cases
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA enforces the Market Abuse Regulation by investigating misconduct and imposing penalties to maintain market integrity.

n.1: Monetary policy does not address market abuse; enforcement does.
n.2: Liquidity support is the Bank’s role, not linked to market abuse enforcement.
n.3: Debt issuance is managed by the DMO, not the FCA.
n.4: Authorisation of clearing banks involves the PRA and FCA jointly, not market abuse enforcement.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which best describes the FCA’s general rule-making duty when proposing significant Handbook changes?
o: Undertake cost-benefit analysis and consult, subject to exceptions
Seek mandatory approval from HM Treasury before consultation
Publish rules without consultation if beneficial to competition
Refer proposals to the PRC for prudential sign-off
Defer to the Bank of England where market liquidity is affected
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA’s rule-making powers include conducting a cost-benefit analysis and consulting stakeholders before making significant rules, with limited exceptions (e.g., urgency).

n.1: Treasury approval is not a blanket prerequisite for FCA consultation.
n.2: Competition benefits do not remove the general consultation duty.
n.3: The PRC does not sign off FCA conduct rules; it oversees PRA prudential policy.
n.4: While coordination can occur, FCA rule-making does not default to Bank sign-off.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK Act consolidated regulation under the FSA before being replaced in 2012?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: FSMA 2000 consolidated financial regulation under the FSA, later reformed by the Financial Services Act 2012 which introduced the FCA and PRA.

n.1: The Banking Act 2009 introduced resolution, not unified regulation.
n.2: The Companies Act covers company law, not regulatory consolidation.
n.3: The Enterprise Act addresses competition, not financial regulation.
n.4: The 2012 Act replaced the FSA with FCA and PRA, but FSMA created the FSA originally.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulator is responsible for approving prospectuses for securities listings in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA approves prospectuses for securities listings, ensuring investor disclosure and market integrity.

n.1: The PRA supervises prudential risk but does not approve prospectuses.
n.2: The Bank does not oversee prospectus approval; this is FCA’s role.
n.3: HM Treasury sets frameworks, but prospectus approvals are FCA responsibilities.
n.4: The CMA handles competition law, not listing prospectuses.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulation governs EU-wide data protection standards?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The GDPR established uniform data protection standards across the EU, with significant implications for financial firms handling client data.

n.1: MiFID II regulates markets and investor protection, not data privacy.
n.2: Solvency II sets insurer solvency standards, not data protection.
n.3: UCITS governs collective funds, not data standards.
n.4: The Banking Act 2009 introduced resolution powers, not data protection.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which FCA objective is most closely linked to promoting confidence in UK financial markets?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA’s statutory objective of market integrity ensures that UK markets are fair, effective, and trusted, thereby underpinning investor confidence.

n.1: Operational resilience is an important supervisory theme but not a statutory objective.
n.2: Safety and soundness is a PRA objective, not the FCA’s.
n.3: Inflation targeting belongs to the MPC, not the FCA.
n.4: Competition is a statutory objective but separate from ensuring market integrity.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which authority monitors UK financial reporting and accounting standards?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Reporting Council oversees corporate reporting, audit quality, and actuarial standards in the UK.

n.1: The FCA supervises conduct in financial services, not accounting standards.
n.2: The Bank focuses on monetary and systemic stability, not corporate reporting.
n.3: The CMA enforces competition law, not accounting standards.
n.4: HM Treasury sets financial legislation, not accounting oversight.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Who is responsible for enforcing the UK’s Competition Act 1998 in financial markets?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces the Competition Act 1998, including in financial services markets, to prevent anti-competitive practices.

n.1: The FCA regulates conduct but does not enforce the Competition Act.
n.2: The PRA focuses on prudential safety, not competition law.
n.3: The Bank of England manages systemic stability, not competition enforcement.
n.4: The FSCS pays compensation to consumers, not enforce competition law.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU regulation harmonises fund management across Europe?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The UCITS Directive harmonises fund regulation, enabling cross-border distribution of mutual funds in the EU.

n.1: Solvency II applies to insurers, not funds.
n.2: MiFID II regulates financial markets, not collective investments.
n.3: PSD regulates payments, not funds.
n.4: GDPR governs data privacy, not fund regulation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body investigates serious and complex fraud affecting financial markets?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Serious Fraud Office investigates serious and complex fraud cases, including those that impact UK financial markets.

n.1: The FCA investigates conduct breaches but does not lead complex fraud prosecutions.
n.2: The CMA focuses on competition enforcement, not fraud.
n.3: The FRC oversees corporate reporting and audit, not fraud cases.
n.4: The PRA supervises prudential soundness, not fraud investigations.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which organisation investigates serious accounting misconduct in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Reporting Council investigates serious accounting and audit misconduct to uphold trust in corporate reporting.

n.1: The FCA focuses on conduct in financial markets, not accounting misconduct.
n.2: The PRA ensures financial soundness, not accounting oversight.
n.3: The Bank of England does not investigate accounting misconduct.
n.4: The CMA enforces competition policy, not accounting.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU regulation governs credit rating agencies operating in Europe?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Credit Rating Agencies Regulation introduced oversight of credit rating agencies, requiring registration and conduct standards to improve transparency.

n.1: MiFID II regulates investment services, not rating agencies.
n.2: Solvency II applies to insurers, not rating agencies.
n.3: UCITS applies to investment funds, not rating agencies.
n.4: GDPR regulates data protection, not credit ratings.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which international body coordinates global AML and CTF measures?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Action Task Force coordinates global efforts to combat money laundering and terrorist financing, issuing recommendations adopted worldwide.

n.1: IOSCO sets securities standards, not AML.
n.2: The Basel Committee sets banking capital standards, not AML.
n.3: The OECD advises on economic policies, not AML.
n.4: The World Bank funds development, not AML frameworks.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What did the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II) aim to enhance?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: MiFID II aimed to improve market transparency, strengthen investor protection, and increase competition in EU financial markets.

n.1: Monetary stability is managed by central banks, not MiFID II.
n.2: Debt issuance is managed by governments and DMOs, not MiFID II.
n.3: Pension funding standards fall under pensions legislation, not MiFID II.
n.4: Global shipping competition is unrelated to MiFID II.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK body ensures compliance with advertising rules in print and digital media?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Advertising Standards Authority regulates print and digital advertising, ensuring financial promotions and adverts are not misleading.

n.1: The FCA regulates financial promotions but relies on the ASA for advertising standards.
n.2: Ofcom regulates broadcast media, not print and digital advertising.
n.3: The PRA oversees prudential soundness, not advertising standards.
n.4: The Bank manages stability, not advertising regulation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK legislation created the Prudential Regulation Authority and Financial Conduct Authority?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Services Act 2012 abolished the FSA and created the FCA and PRA within the twin-peaks model.

n.1: The Banking Act 2009 introduced resolution powers, not FCA/PRA creation.
n.2: The Companies Act governs company law, not financial regulators.
n.3: The Enterprise Act concerns competition, not financial regulation bodies.
n.4: The Bribery Act addresses corruption, not regulators.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body provides oversight of corporate reporting in listed companies?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FRC monitors corporate reporting of listed companies to maintain transparency and investor confidence in financial markets.

n.1: The FCA enforces conduct in markets but does not oversee detailed reporting standards.
n.2: The Bank ensures stability, not corporate reporting.
n.3: The CMA enforces competition, not reporting standards.
n.4: The PRA supervises prudential safety, not corporate reporting.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK statutory instrument transferred EU financial directives into domestic law post-Brexit?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018 converted EU law, including financial directives, into UK domestic law after Brexit.

n.1: FSMA 2000 provides the overall framework but not the Brexit transition mechanism.
n.2: The Banking Act 2009 deals with resolution powers, not EU law transposition.
n.3: The Companies Act 2006 governs company law, not EU withdrawal.
n.4: The Enterprise Act covers competition and insolvency, not EU law transfer.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the Bank of England’s resolution objective under the Banking Act 2009?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Bank’s resolution objective is to protect and enhance financial stability while minimising public costs and ensuring continuity of critical services.

n.1: Resolution does not guarantee profitability; it focuses on stability.
n.2: Consumer protection is the FCA’s remit, not the Bank’s resolution objective.
n.3: Listing approvals are FCA tasks, not Bank resolution duties.
n.4: Borrowing is managed by HM Treasury and DMO, not the Bank’s resolution directorate.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK Act enhanced the accountability of the Bank of England after the 2008 crisis?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Services Act 2012 restructured regulation post-crisis, increasing Bank of England accountability and creating the FCA and PRA.

n.1: The Banking Act 2009 introduced resolution tools but not FCA/PRA creation.
n.2: The Companies Act is corporate law, not financial regulation.
n.3: The Enterprise Act covers competition and insolvency, not central bank reform.
n.4: FSMA 2000 is the original framework but was reformed in 2012.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body oversees the professional conduct of barristers in England and Wales?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Bar Standards Board regulates barristers and specialised legal services, ensuring professional conduct and competence.

n.1: The SRA regulates solicitors, not barristers.
n.2: The FCA regulates financial firms, not barristers.
n.3: The actuarial profession is regulated by the IFoA, not the BSB.
n.4: The CMA enforces competition law, not barristers’ conduct.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the PRA’s approach to authorisation under FSMA?
o: Assess prudential soundness before granting permission
Ensure best product pricing for retail customers
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: When authorising firms, the PRA assesses whether they meet prudential threshold conditions to ensure financial soundness and resilience.

n.1: Product pricing is an FCA conduct issue, not PRA authorisation.
n.2: Fines are enforcement outcomes, not part of PRA authorisation.
n.3: IPO prospectuses are FCA’s responsibility, not PRA’s.
n.4: Fiscal policy decisions sit with HM Treasury, not PRA.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which global organisation promotes investor protection and fair securities markets?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: IOSCO promotes global standards for securities regulation, focusing on investor protection, market fairness, and reducing systemic risk.

n.1: The Basel Committee issues banking standards, not securities regulation.
n.2: The IMF promotes financial stability but not securities regulation directly.
n.3: The World Bank supports development projects, not securities oversight.
n.4: The OECD develops economic policy guidelines, not securities regulation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Who investigates market misconduct that may breach criminal law in addition to FCA enforcement?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Serious Fraud Office can prosecute market misconduct when it constitutes serious criminal fraud beyond regulatory enforcement by the FCA.

n.1: The ICO enforces data protection laws, not financial crime.
n.2: The FRC regulates audits and reporting, not market crime.
n.3: The PRA focuses on prudential supervision, not criminal law.
n.4: HM Treasury sets the framework, not enforcement.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body enforces insider trading offences under criminal law?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Serious Fraud Office investigates and prosecutes insider trading when it constitutes serious criminal activity.

n.1: The FCA enforces regulatory and civil sanctions, but serious criminal prosecutions fall to the SFO.
n.2: The PRA regulates prudential soundness, not criminal insider trading.
n.3: The Bank ensures systemic stability, not criminal enforcement.
n.4: The Insolvency Service investigates insolvencies, not insider trading.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU regulation governs transparency in securities financing transactions?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The SFTR introduced transparency rules for securities lending and repos, requiring reporting to trade repositories.

n.1: MiFID II governs conduct rules, not securities financing.
n.2: UCITS governs collective investment schemes, not securities financing.
n.3: Solvency II applies to insurers, not repo markets.
n.4: PSD2 regulates payment services, not securities financing.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which directive harmonises investor protection and conduct standards across Europe?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: MiFID II harmonises investor protection and conduct standards across EU financial markets, enhancing transparency and investor rights.

n.1: Solvency II governs insurers, not investor conduct.
n.2: UCITS regulates investment funds, not investor conduct broadly.
n.3: PSD2 governs payments, not investor conduct.
n.4: BRRD governs bank recovery, not conduct rules.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which authority investigates cartel behaviour in the UK financial sector?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The CMA investigates and takes enforcement action against cartel behaviour across sectors, including financial services.

n.1: The FCA regulates conduct but does not lead cartel enforcement.
n.2: The PRA regulates prudential safety, not cartels.
n.3: The FOS resolves disputes, not cartel investigations.
n.4: The Bank ensures systemic stability, not competition enforcement.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body supervises UK competition in retail banking services?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Competition and Markets Authority investigates and acts against anti-competitive practices, including in retail banking services.

n.1: The FCA regulates conduct and disclosure, not competition law.
n.2: The Bank focuses on monetary stability, not competition.
n.3: The PRA oversees prudential soundness, not competition.
n.4: The Insolvency Service investigates insolvencies, not competition.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Who issues the statutory ‘remit and recommendations’ letters that guide the regulators’ priorities?
o: HM Treasury to FCA, PRA and the Bank committees
FCA Board to PRA and Bank committees
Bank of England Court to HM Treasury
Competition and Markets Authority to FCA
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: HM Treasury periodically sends remit and recommendations letters setting out strategic priorities and expectations for the FCA, PRA and certain Bank committees, aligning regulatory focus with wider economic policy.

n.1: The FCA receives guidance; it does not issue such Treasury letters to other bodies.
n.2: The Court manages Bank governance; remit letters originate from the Treasury.
n.3: The CMA may coordinate on competition policy but does not issue Treasury remits.
n.4: The NAO audits value for money; remit letters are not its function.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which global standard-setter issues Basel banking accords?
o: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision issues the Basel Accords, which set international standards for bank capital and risk management.

n.1: The IMF supports global financial stability but does not issue Basel accords.
n.2: The World Bank funds development projects, not banking capital standards.
n.3: The ECB sets monetary policy for the eurozone, not global prudential standards.
n.4: The OECD focuses on economic policy, not banking regulation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body regulates actuaries’ professional and ethical standards?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Institute and Faculty of Actuaries sets professional and ethical standards for the actuarial profession in the UK.

n.1: The FRC oversees audit and reporting standards, not professional actuarial ethics.
n.2: The FCA regulates conduct in financial markets, not actuarial ethics.
n.3: The PRA supervises prudential safety of firms, not actuaries.
n.4: The Bank manages systemic stability, not actuaries’ standards.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulator enforces the UK Bribery Act in financial services?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Serious Fraud Office prosecutes offences under the Bribery Act, including in financial services, where bribery constitutes serious criminal conduct.

n.1: The FCA enforces conduct rules but does not prosecute bribery under criminal law.
n.2: The PRA focuses on prudential supervision, not bribery.
n.3: The CMA enforces competition, not bribery law.
n.4: The ICO enforces data protection, not bribery offences.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which authority oversees professional standards in the insurance broking industry?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Chartered Insurance Institute is the professional body for insurance and financial planning, setting ethical and educational standards for brokers and advisers.

n.1: The FCA regulates conduct of insurance brokers, but professional standards sit with the CII.
n.2: The PRA supervises prudential safety of insurers, not brokers’ professional conduct.
n.3: The Bank of England focuses on systemic stability, not broker qualifications.
n.4: The CMA enforces competition law, not insurance professional standards.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which statutory body is responsible for consumer credit regulation after the transfer from the OFT?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: Consumer credit regulation transferred from the Office of Fair Trading to the FCA in 2014, making it responsible for authorisation and supervision in this sector.

n.1: The PRA focuses on prudential soundness of banks and insurers, not consumer credit.
n.2: The Bank oversees monetary and systemic stability, not consumer credit conduct.
n.3: The CMA handles competition, not regulatory authorisation of consumer credit firms.
n.4: HM Treasury sets legislation but does not supervise credit firms directly.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: For a new bank application under Part 4A FSMA, which combination is required?
o: PRA authorisation decision with FCA consent
FCA authorisation decision with PRA consent
HM Treasury approval followed by FCA licence
Bank of England Court approval then PRA consent
Competition and Markets Authority clearance then FCA licence
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: Dual-regulated entities like banks are authorised by the PRA for prudential purposes, but the PRA must obtain the FCA’s consent on conduct considerations before granting Part 4A permission.

n.1: For banks, the FCA cannot be the lead decision-maker; the PRA is primary with FCA consent.
n.2: Treasury does not approve individual licences; it sets the legislative framework.
n.3: The Court oversees governance; it does not approve individual firm authorisations.
n.4: CMA clearance may be relevant to competition issues but is separate from FSMA authorisation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulator monitors auditors of listed UK companies?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FRC oversees the regulation and monitoring of auditors to maintain standards in listed company audits.

n.1: The FCA enforces market conduct, not audit oversight.
n.2: The Bank of England manages stability, not audit regulation.
n.3: The PRA supervises prudential soundness, not auditors.
n.4: The CMA enforces competition law, not auditor monitoring.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulator monitors unfair contract terms in consumer finance?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Competition and Markets Authority has powers to investigate and enforce against unfair contract terms, including those used in consumer finance markets.

n.1: The FCA regulates disclosure and conduct but unfair terms enforcement sits with the CMA.
n.2: The PRA supervises prudential matters, not contracts.
n.3: The FRC oversees corporate reporting, not contract fairness.
n.4: The Bank ensures stability, not consumer contract terms.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body has oversight of UK occupational pension scheme funding standards?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Pensions Regulator ensures that occupational pension schemes are funded appropriately to protect members’ benefits.

n.1: The FCA focuses on conduct in financial markets, not pension funding.
n.2: The PRA supervises insurers and banks, not pension schemes.
n.3: The FRC oversees reporting and audit standards, not pension funding.
n.4: The SFO prosecutes serious fraud, not pension funding oversight.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive harmonises rules for packaged retail and insurance-based investment products?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The PRIIPs Regulation sets disclosure standards for packaged retail and insurance-based investment products to improve comparability and transparency.

n.1: MiFID II governs market conduct, not PRIIPs disclosure.
n.2: UCITS applies to collective funds, not PRIIPs broadly.
n.3: Solvency II covers insurers’ prudential rules, not disclosure documents.
n.4: PSD2 governs payment services, not investment product disclosures.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK authority is responsible for implementing EU directives into national law pre-Brexit?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: HM Treasury had responsibility for transposing EU directives into UK law, working with regulators to implement detailed rules.

n.1: The FCA enforces and applies directives but Treasury transposes them into law.
n.2: The Bank provides systemic stability but does not transpose directives.
n.3: The PRA supervises prudential firms, not legislative transposition.
n.4: The CMA enforces competition, not EU law transposition.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulator authorises UK actuaries?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Institute and Faculty of Actuaries regulates its members, setting professional standards and authorising actuaries.

n.1: The FRC sets standards but does not individually authorise actuaries.
n.2: The FCA does not regulate the actuarial profession.
n.3: The PRA supervises insurers that employ actuaries, not the profession itself.
n.4: HM Treasury does not regulate actuaries directly.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which FCA division oversees the UK Listing Authority function?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA’s Markets division operates the UK Listing Authority function, overseeing issuers, disclosure and market integrity.

n.1: The PRA’s prudential division supervises firm safety, not listings.
n.2: Resolution is the Bank’s remit, not FCA listings.
n.3: The DMO manages government debt issuance, not listing approvals.
n.4: The CMA manages competition, not listing authority functions.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which professional body sets standards for chartered financial planners in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Chartered Insurance Institute awards chartered status and sets professional standards for financial planners and advisers.

n.1: The FCA regulates conduct but does not award chartered status.
n.2: The IFoA regulates actuaries, not financial planners.
n.3: The Bank manages systemic stability, not financial planning standards.
n.4: The CMA enforces competition, not professional qualifications.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which organisation coordinates global financial stability initiatives?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Stability Board coordinates at international level to monitor and make recommendations about the global financial system.

n.1: IOSCO sets securities standards, not overall financial stability.
n.2: The Basel Committee sets bank standards, not overall coordination.
n.3: The IMF supports financial stability but the FSB coordinates standards globally.
n.4: The World Bank funds development, not global financial regulation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body oversees anti-money laundering supervision for solicitors in England and Wales?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Solicitors Regulation Authority supervises anti-money laundering compliance for law firms under the Money Laundering Regulations.

n.1: The FCA supervises financial firms, not solicitors.
n.2: The PRA oversees prudential soundness of banks and insurers, not legal practices.
n.3: HM Treasury sets policy but does not supervise solicitors’ AML compliance.
n.4: The CMA oversees competition policy, not AML for solicitors.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulator monitors competition in wholesale financial markets?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The CMA investigates and enforces competition issues across all markets, including wholesale financial markets.

n.1: The FCA enforces conduct rules, not competition law.
n.2: The PRA ensures prudential soundness, not competition.
n.3: The FOS handles disputes, not market competition.
n.4: The Bank oversees systemic stability, not competition enforcement.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulator oversees auditors and audit quality in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Reporting Council regulates auditors and monitors audit quality to promote high standards of corporate governance.

n.1: The FCA oversees financial markets conduct, not audits.
n.2: The CMA enforces competition law, not audit quality.
n.3: The Bank focuses on systemic stability, not audits.
n.4: The PRA supervises prudential risks, not auditor oversight.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body oversees monetary stability in the UK?
o: Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Committee
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Committee manages monetary stability, primarily by setting interest rates and controlling inflation.

n.1: The FCA oversees conduct and market integrity, not monetary stability.
n.2: The PRA manages prudential soundness, not monetary stability.
n.3: HM Treasury sets the policy framework but does not directly control monetary stability.
n.4: The CMA enforces competition policy, not monetary stability.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What does the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) introduce in EU regulation?
o: Open banking and third-party payment access
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: PSD2 introduced open banking, requiring banks to provide third-party access to payment accounts to encourage innovation and competition.

n.1: Prudential insurance rules are in Solvency II, not PSD2.
n.2: Bank capital requirements are covered by Basel and CRD, not PSD2.
n.3: Corporate governance codes are separate from payment regulation.
n.4: Credit rating agencies are covered by separate EU regulation, not PSD2.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive regulates the marketing of alternative investment funds?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive regulates hedge funds, private equity, and other non-UCITS investment funds marketed in the EU.

n.1: UCITS governs mutual funds, not alternative funds.
n.2: MiFID II covers investment services, not alternative funds specifically.
n.3: Solvency II applies to insurers, not fund managers.
n.4: PSD2 regulates payments, not fund managers.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the role of the Takeover Panel?
o: Oversee compliance with the Takeover Code
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Takeover Panel administers and enforces the UK Takeover Code to ensure fair treatment of shareholders during mergers and acquisitions.

n.1: Insurer solvency is a PRA responsibility, not the Takeover Panel.
n.2: The FCA enforces conduct rules, not the Panel.
n.3: Remit letters are issued by HM Treasury, not the Takeover Panel.
n.4: Monetary policy is set by the MPC, not the Panel.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which organisation oversees professional standards of accountants in the UK?
o: Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales (ICAEW) regulates its members and sets professional standards for accountants.

n.1: The FCA regulates conduct in financial markets, not accountants directly.
n.2: The PRA regulates prudential safety, not accounting standards.
n.3: The Bank of England manages systemic risks, not accountant qualifications.
n.4: HM Treasury sets legislation but does not regulate accountants.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which organisation oversees the UK Corporate Governance Code?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Reporting Council monitors compliance with the UK Corporate Governance Code to improve accountability and transparency in listed companies.

n.1: The FCA enforces listing rules but does not oversee the Code.
n.2: The Bank manages stability, not governance codes.
n.3: The CMA handles competition issues, not governance codes.
n.4: HM Treasury sets the framework but does not administer the Code.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Where does legal authority for UK monetary policy decisions sit?
o: Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Committee
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The MPC within the Bank of England has statutory authority for monetary policy decisions.

n.1: HM Treasury sets the framework and accountability, while the MPC makes monetary decisions.
n.2: The FCA Board oversees conduct regulation, not monetary policy set by the MPC.
n.3: The PRC oversees prudential regulation, whereas monetary policy is set by the MPC.
n.4: The DMO manages government debt issuance, not interest-rate policy set by the MPC.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulator oversees consumer credit agreements under UK law?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA regulates consumer credit, ensuring agreements are fair and firms treat customers appropriately.

n.1: The PRA oversees prudential risks, not consumer credit.
n.2: The Bank ensures systemic stability, not credit agreements.
n.3: The CMA enforces competition, not consumer credit law.
n.4: The FRC oversees reporting and auditing, not credit regulation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU regulation improved transparency in derivatives markets?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The European Market Infrastructure Regulation (EMIR) introduced central clearing, reporting, and risk mitigation for OTC derivatives.

n.1: MiFID II governs securities markets, not derivatives clearing.
n.2: UCITS covers investment funds, not derivatives markets.
n.3: PSD2 regulates payments, not derivatives.
n.4: Solvency II applies to insurers, not derivatives.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which obligation most directly reflects the FCA’s consumer protection role?
o: Assess product value and fair outcomes across distribution
Set countercyclical capital buffers at systemic level
Act as resolution authority for failing banks
Set the base rate to meet the inflation target
Determine liquidity assistance terms for solvent firms
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA’s consumer protection objective drives requirements on fair value, distribution oversight and avoiding foreseeable harm, ensuring that products deliver suitable outcomes across their lifecycle.

n.1: System-level buffers are set by the FPC, not the FCA.
n.2: Resolution is led by the Bank of England, not the FCA.
n.3: Interest-rate setting is the MPC’s role.
n.4: Liquidity assistance terms are part of the Bank’s market operations.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the main role of the Financial Ombudsman Service?
o: Resolve disputes between consumers and financial firms
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Ombudsman Service provides impartial dispute resolution for consumers and financial firms outside the courts.

n.1: Capital requirements are set by the PRA, not the Ombudsman.
n.2: Trustees are overseen by The Pensions Regulator, not FOS.
n.3: Debt issuance is handled by the DMO, not FOS.
n.4: Data protection is enforced by the ICO, not FOS.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive created investor protection and conduct of business rules?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: MiFID II created comprehensive investor protection and conduct rules for investment firms, improving transparency and consumer safeguards.

n.1: Solvency II applies to insurers, not investor conduct.
n.2: UCITS governs investment funds, not conduct standards broadly.
n.3: PSD2 regulates payments, not investor conduct.
n.4: BRRD governs bank recovery, not conduct rules.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Who decides authorisation for a new UK bank?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: Dual-regulated firms are authorised by the PRA with the FCA’s consent for conduct considerations.

n.1: The FCA cannot authorise a bank alone, since the PRA is the prudential decision-maker.
n.2: The Court oversees Bank governance, while authorisation decisions rest with the PRA and FCA.
n.3: HM Treasury sets the framework but does not approve individual bank authorisations.
n.4: The CMA handles competition issues, not prudential authorisations for new banks.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive sets prudential standards for insurers?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Solvency II Directive provides harmonised prudential regulation for insurers, covering capital, governance, and risk management.

n.1: MiFID II regulates investment firm conduct, not insurers.
n.2: UCITS covers collective investment schemes, not insurers.
n.3: BRRD applies to banks, not insurers.
n.4: PSD2 governs payment services, not insurers.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the main responsibility of the Prudential Regulation Authority?
o: Ensure the safety and soundness of firms it regulates
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The PRA’s primary responsibility is to promote the safety and soundness of banks, building societies, credit unions, insurers and major investment firms.

n.1: Consumer protection against promotions is an FCA role.
n.2: National economic policy is managed by HM Treasury, not the PRA.
n.3: Prospectus approval is the FCA’s role, not the PRA’s.
n.4: Borrowing is managed by the DMO under Treasury, not the PRA.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK body regulates occupational pension schemes’ governance standards?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Pensions Regulator ensures occupational pension schemes have proper governance, protecting scheme members’ benefits.

n.1: The FCA oversees personal pension conduct, not occupational governance.
n.2: The Bank focuses on systemic stability, not pensions governance.
n.3: The CMA enforces competition, not pension governance.
n.4: The FRC oversees reporting and audit, not pension scheme governance.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which directive introduced investor compensation schemes across the EU?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Investor Compensation Schemes Directive requires member states to have schemes protecting investors if firms fail to return assets.

n.1: MiFID II governs markets and conduct, not investor compensation.
n.2: UCITS covers collective funds, not compensation schemes.
n.3: Solvency II applies to insurers, not compensation.
n.4: BRRD applies to banks’ recovery and resolution, not investor compensation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Who is responsible for setting the UK’s overall economic strategy?
o: Bank of England’s Court of Directors
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: HM Treasury is responsible for fiscal and economic strategy, working with regulators to ensure alignment with government policy.

n.1: The FCA regulates conduct but does not set national economic strategy.
n.2: The PRA supervises prudential risks, not economic strategy.
n.3: The Court manages Bank governance, not economic strategy.
n.4: The FPC targets systemic risk, not overall economic strategy.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the primary purpose of the UCITS Directive?
o: Regulate collective investment schemes across the EU
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The UCITS Directive provides a harmonised framework for collective investment schemes, enabling cross-border distribution within the EU.

n.1: Prudential standards for banks are set by Basel and CRD, not UCITS.
n.2: Insurance solvency is governed by Solvency II, not UCITS.
n.3: Electronic payments are covered under the PSD, not UCITS.
n.4: Corporate governance standards are overseen by codes and the FRC, not UCITS.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which Bank of England committee decides the level of the UK’s official Bank Rate?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The MPC sets the official Bank Rate to achieve the government’s inflation target and ensure monetary stability.

n.1: The FPC sets macroprudential tools, not interest rates.
n.2: The PRC oversees prudential regulation, not interest rates.
n.3: The Court manages governance, not monetary policy.
n.4: Resolution is a Bank function, but interest rates are set by the MPC.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which organisation investigates company insolvencies in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Insolvency Service investigates insolvencies and director misconduct, supporting the UK insolvency regime.

n.1: The FCA regulates conduct, not company insolvency.
n.2: The PRA supervises financial soundness of firms, not insolvencies.
n.3: The CMA deals with competition, not insolvency.
n.4: The FRC sets accounting and audit standards, not insolvency investigations.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body provides oversight of occupational pension scheme trustees?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Pensions Regulator oversees pension scheme trustees to ensure schemes are funded and governed properly.

n.1: The FCA supervises personal pensions and conduct, not scheme trustees.
n.2: The Bank does not oversee pension trustees.
n.3: The CMA enforces competition, not pensions.
n.4: The SFO investigates fraud, not pension governance.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive governs electronic money institutions?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Electronic Money Directive regulates e-money institutions, covering issuance, safeguarding of funds, and capital requirements.

n.1: Solvency II covers insurers, not e-money firms.
n.2: UCITS applies to investment funds, not e-money.
n.3: BRRD applies to bank resolution, not e-money.
n.4: GDPR governs data privacy, not e-money institutions.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK body investigates cartel activity involving banks?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The CMA investigates and prosecutes anti-competitive practices such as cartels, including those in banking markets.

n.1: The FCA regulates conduct but does not prosecute cartels.
n.2: The Bank oversees financial stability, not cartel activity.
n.3: The PRA supervises prudential soundness, not competition law.
n.4: The SFO prosecutes fraud and corruption, not competition cartels.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the PRA’s approach to setting requirements for an insurer’s own funds?
o: Risk-based prudential standards aligned to Solvency II framework
Uniform leverage ratio identical to retail banks
Product intervention to cap premiums for vulnerable customers
Listing rule waivers tied to capital issuance plans
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: For insurers, the PRA applies a risk-based prudential regime aligned to Solvency II concepts (e.g., own funds quality and capital requirements), focusing on policyholder protection and firm safety and soundness.

n.1: A bank-style leverage ratio is not uniformly applied to insurers given different risk profiles and regimes.
n.2: Premium caps are a conduct matter; the PRA focuses on prudential soundness.
n.3: Monetary policy tools are within the MPC’s remit, not PRA capital setting.
n.4: Listing rules are overseen by the FCA, not tied to PRA capital decisions.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which organisation ensures auditors remain independent from the firms they audit?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Reporting Council ensures auditors maintain independence, safeguarding the credibility of corporate audits.

n.1: The FCA oversees market conduct, not auditor independence.
n.2: The PRA supervises prudential soundness, not auditors.
n.3: HM Treasury sets policy but does not regulate auditor independence.
n.4: The CMA addresses competition concerns, not auditor independence.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which framework requires UK banks to prepare ‘living wills’?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Banking Act 2009 introduced recovery and resolution planning, requiring banks to prepare ‘living wills’ for orderly wind-down if needed.

n.1: MiFID II governs markets and investor protection, not living wills.
n.2: Solvency II applies to insurers, not banks.
n.3: UCITS covers investment funds, not bank recovery plans.
n.4: GDPR governs data protection, not bank resolution.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which statement best describes HM Treasury’s accountability to Parliament?
o: It is accountable for the overall regulatory framework and policy direction
It is responsible for daily supervision of firms
It must enforce conduct fines directly
It determines every enforcement investigation outcome
It sets capital adequacy for dual-regulated firms
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: HM Treasury is accountable to Parliament for the statutory and policy framework governing financial regulation.

n.1: Day-to-day supervision is handled by FCA and PRA, not Treasury.
n.2: Fines are imposed by regulators, not Treasury.
n.3: Enforcement outcomes are decided by regulators, not Treasury.
n.4: Capital adequacy is the PRA’s role, not Treasury’s.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What role does the PRA play in the Bank of England’s overall structure?
o: Acts as a ring-fenced regulatory arm for prudential supervision
Sets fiscal policy for the government
Administers conduct rules for all investment firms
Directly manages equity trading on UK exchanges
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The PRA functions as part of the Bank of England, operating as its prudential regulator for banks, insurers and systemically important firms, with its policy overseen by the Prudential Regulation Committee.

n.1: Fiscal policy is managed by the government and HM Treasury, not the PRA.
n.2: Conduct rules for investment firms are FCA responsibilities, not PRA.
n.3: Debt issuance is managed by the DMO, not PRA.
n.4: Equity trading oversight is FCA’s market integrity remit, not PRA.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Why might the FCA deploy temporary product intervention rules?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA can intervene temporarily where products pose a serious risk of consumer harm.

n.1: Inflation targeting is for the MPC, whereas FCA interventions address consumer detriment.
n.2: Systemic liquidity is handled by the Bank of England, while FCA tools protect consumers.
n.3: Borrowing requirements are Treasury matters, not grounds for FCA product interventions.
n.4: Licensing banks involves PRA consent with FCA input, not temporary FCA product bans.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the PRA’s primary statutory objective?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The PRA’s core objective is promoting the safety and soundness of regulated firms.

n.1: Consumer outcomes are the FCA’s conduct focus, whereas the PRA’s remit is prudential safety.
n.2: Low, stable inflation is targeted by the MPC, not the PRA’s prudential objective.
n.3: Competition objectives sit with the FCA, while the PRA focuses on firm resilience.
n.4: Managing the national debt is handled by the Debt Management Office, not the PRA.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU regulation strengthened data protection rules for financial firms?
o: Markets in Financial Instruments Directive II
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) imposed strict rules on data handling and privacy, directly impacting financial firms’ operations.

n.1: MiFID II focuses on markets and investor protection, not data privacy.
n.2: Solvency II governs insurers’ prudential standards, not data.
n.3: UCITS applies to collective investment schemes, not data protection.
n.4: Basel III sets banking capital rules, not data protection.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which FCA statutory objective ensures consumers are provided with appropriate products and services?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA’s consumer protection objective requires it to ensure that markets deliver products and services that meet consumers’ needs and protect them from harm.

n.1: Market integrity relates to confidence and fairness in markets, not directly to consumer protection.
n.2: Financial stability is a Bank of England and FPC focus, not an FCA objective.
n.3: Inflation control is the MPC’s remit.
n.4: Debt management is carried out by the Debt Management Office, not the FCA.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK Act gave statutory effect to ring-fencing rules separating retail and investment banking?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Services (Banking Reform) Act 2013 gave statutory effect to ring-fencing requirements, separating retail banking from riskier investment banking activities.

n.1: The 2012 Act created the FCA and PRA but did not implement ring-fencing.
n.2: The Banking Act 2009 introduced resolution powers, not ring-fencing.
n.3: The Companies Act governs company law, not bank ring-fencing.
n.4: The Enterprise Act focuses on competition and insolvency, not ring-fencing.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK Act gave regulators stronger powers to ring-fence retail banking operations?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Services (Banking Reform) Act 2013 implemented ring-fencing of retail banking from investment banking to reduce systemic risk.

n.1: FSMA is the overarching framework, but ring-fencing was introduced in 2013 legislation.
n.2: The Companies Act governs company law, not ring-fencing.
n.3: The Enterprise Act relates to competition and insolvency, not ring-fencing.
n.4: The Banking Act 2009 established resolution tools, not ring-fencing.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the purpose of the EU Capital Requirements Directive (CRD IV)?
o: Implement Basel III standards into EU law
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: CRD IV transposed Basel III banking standards into EU law, including capital adequacy, liquidity and leverage requirements.

n.1: Open banking was introduced under PSD2, not CRD IV.
n.2: MiFID II, not CRD IV, focuses on investor protection.
n.3: Solvency II covers insurance, not CRD IV.
n.4: UCITS governs investment funds, not CRD IV.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulator is primarily concerned with ensuring fair treatment of customers?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA’s remit is conduct regulation, which includes ensuring fair treatment of customers across financial services.

n.1: The PRA focuses on prudential soundness, not customer conduct.
n.2: The Bank’s remit covers monetary and systemic stability, not consumer outcomes.
n.3: HM Treasury sets policy frameworks but does not regulate firm conduct.
n.4: The FPC focuses on system-wide risks, not customer conduct.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What does the FCA’s competition objective require it to do?
o: Promote effective competition in the interests of consumers
Guarantee market stability at all times
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA’s competition objective requires it to promote effective competition in the interests of consumers, ensuring better choice and outcomes in financial services markets.

n.1: Regulatory objectives are not designed to maximise firm profits.
n.2: Market stability is a Bank of England role, not an FCA competition objective.
n.3: Lender-of-last-resort facilities are provided by the Bank of England, not the FCA.
n.4: Bond issuance is managed by the DMO under Treasury, not FCA.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive aimed to strengthen bank capital and liquidity post-crisis?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: CRD IV transposed Basel III requirements into EU law, strengthening banks’ capital and liquidity standards.

n.1: MiFID II focuses on conduct, not capital requirements.
n.2: UCITS governs funds, not bank capital.
n.3: Solvency II applies to insurers, not banks.
n.4: GDPR regulates data protection, not bank capital rules.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive created a single passport for investment firms across member states?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: MiFID established the passport system allowing investment firms authorised in one EU state to operate across others without separate licences.

n.1: Solvency II focuses on insurers’ capital, not investment passports.
n.2: BRRD concerns bank recovery and resolution, not cross-border services.
n.3: PSD regulates payments, not investment services.
n.4: GDPR governs data protection, not market passports.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body within the Bank of England sets system-wide macroprudential policy other than resolution execution?
o: Court of the Bank of England
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: Macroprudential policy, such as sectoral capital requirements and the countercyclical buffer, is set by the Financial Policy Committee to address system-wide risks. Resolution execution is led by the Bank as resolution authority, which is separate from the FPC’s policy function.

n.1: The PRC oversees prudential regulation of firms (PRA) rather than system-wide macroprudential tools.
n.2: The MPC targets price stability via monetary policy, not macroprudential buffers.
n.3: The Court is the Bank’s governing board and does not set macroprudential policy.
n.4: There is no separate PRA Supervisory Board setting macroprudential policy; the FPC holds that remit.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Under the UK’s twin-peaks model, which statement best describes the split between the FCA and PRA?
o: FCA leads conduct; PRA leads prudential for deposit-takers and insurers
FCA leads prudential; PRA leads conduct for dual-regulated firms
Both share equal conduct responsibilities for all authorised firms
PRA handles market abuse; FCA handles capital adequacy
PRA authorises all firms; FCA supervises all firms
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The model assigns the FCA to conduct regulation across the market, while the PRA performs prudential regulation for systemically important sectors such as banks, building societies and insurers. Many large firms are dual-regulated: PRA for prudential, FCA for conduct.

n.1: Prudential supervision of major firms is the PRA’s role, not the FCA’s.
n.2: Conduct is not joint by default; the FCA is the conduct regulator.
n.3: Market abuse enforcement sits with the FCA; prudential capital sits with the PRA for dual-regulated firms.
n.4: Authorisation is split: PRA authorises dual-regulated firms with FCA consent; FCA authorises solo-regulated firms.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Following the Financial Services and Markets Act reforms, what additional emphasis do the FCA and PRA share beyond their primary objectives?
o: A secondary objective to facilitate growth and international competitiveness
A joint duty to set interest rates during crises
A primary objective to maximise regulator fee income
A requirement to approve all mergers above a set threshold
A mandate to provide liquidity directly to investment funds
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: Recent reforms added a secondary objective for both regulators to facilitate the UK’s economic growth and international competitiveness, to be advanced in a way that aligns with their primary objectives (consumer protection, market integrity, safety and soundness).

n.1: Interest-rate setting remains with the MPC, not the conduct or prudential regulators.
n.2: Regulators’ objectives are not framed around fee maximisation.
n.3: Merger control primarily sits with the CMA; regulators may give input where relevant.
n.4: Liquidity provision is the Bank of England’s role under specific facilities, not FCA/PRA.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which international agreement established standards on over-the-counter derivatives markets?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The G20 Pittsburgh Summit in 2009 agreed reforms to regulate OTC derivatives, including mandatory clearing and reporting.

n.1: Basel II covers bank capital adequacy, not derivatives reforms.
n.2: OECD corporate governance principles focus on company boards, not derivatives.
n.3: The WTO Doha Round focused on trade, not derivatives regulation.
n.4: IMF SDRs relate to currency reserves, not derivatives.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which global body coordinates prudential supervision standards for banks?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision develops global standards on bank capital adequacy, stress testing, and liquidity.

n.1: IOSCO sets securities regulation standards, not banking prudential rules.
n.2: FATF leads AML, not bank capital.
n.3: The IMF monitors financial stability but does not set prudential bank standards.
n.4: The OECD advises on economic policy, not bank prudential standards.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: How does the Bank of England support solvent banks during liquidity stress?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Bank of England provides liquidity through lender-of-last-resort facilities to solvent firms.

n.1: Sales conduct restrictions are FCA measures, whereas liquidity support is provided by the Bank.
n.2: Product value metrics relate to FCA consumer outcomes, not liquidity backstops.
n.3: Tax rates are Treasury and Parliament matters, not Bank liquidity operations.
n.4: Listing approvals are FCA responsibilities, while the Bank provides liquidity support.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What is the Bank of England’s role in relation to payment systems under the Banking Act 2009?
o: Recognise and supervise systemically important payment systems
Impose conduct fines on payment service providers
Set statutory minimum fees for payments
Provide FSCS compensation for payment delays
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Bank of England recognises and supervises systemically important payment systems, ensuring resilience and stability in UK financial infrastructure.

n.1: Conduct fines fall within the FCA’s remit, not the Bank’s role in payment systems.
n.2: The Bank does not set mandatory minimum fees; market pricing is outside its statutory function.
n.3: Product design approvals are not part of the Bank’s remit; it supervises systemic risk.
n.4: The FSCS covers deposits and certain investments, not compensation for payment system delays.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive regulates payment service providers such as fintechs?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: PSD2 regulates payment services and introduced open banking, requiring fintechs and banks to provide third-party access to payment accounts.

n.1: MiFID II governs investment firms, not payment providers.
n.2: UCITS regulates investment funds, not payments.
n.3: Solvency II applies to insurers, not payments.
n.4: GDPR regulates data, not payment providers.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which EU directive regulates payment institutions and e-money firms?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Payment Services Directive sets regulatory standards for payment institutions and e-money firms, encouraging innovation and consumer protection.

n.1: Solvency II applies to insurers, not payment firms.
n.2: MiFID II governs investment firms, not payments.
n.3: UCITS regulates funds, not payment institutions.
n.4: GDPR regulates data privacy, not payments.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which authority sets professional and ethical standards for chartered accountants?
o: Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The ICAEW is the professional body that sets ethical and professional standards for its members, ensuring quality in the accountancy profession.

n.1: The FCA regulates financial conduct, not the accountancy profession.
n.2: The Bank ensures systemic stability, not professional accountancy standards.
n.3: The FRC oversees audit quality but ICAEW sets member standards.
n.4: The CMA enforces competition law, not professional standards for accountants.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: In what way does the FCA coordinate with the PRA when supervising dual-regulated firms?
o: Sharing responsibility for systemic liquidity injections
Conducting combined inspections for every firm
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA and PRA operate under a Memorandum of Understanding that sets out coordination arrangements for dual-regulated firms, ensuring clarity of responsibilities and reducing duplication.

n.1: Base rates are set by the MPC, not by FCA or PRA jointly.
n.2: Systemic liquidity is a Bank of England role, not FCA or PRA.
n.3: They do not conduct joint inspections by default; coordination is managed case by case.
n.4: Enforcement fines are issued independently, not approved by the other regulator.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulator enforces data protection breaches that impact consumer credit records?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Information Commissioner’s Office enforces data protection laws across sectors, including misuse of consumer credit records.

n.1: The FCA regulates conduct but does not enforce data protection breaches.
n.2: The PRA focuses on prudential safety, not data breaches.
n.3: The CMA enforces competition law, not data protection.
n.4: The Bank of England ensures financial stability, not data protection.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What body acts as the UK resolution authority for failing banks?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Bank of England is the UK resolution authority responsible for executing resolution tools.

n.1: The FCA focuses on conduct; resolution execution is led by the Bank of England.
n.2: HM Treasury may make certain directions, but the Bank executes resolution.
n.3: The PRA supervises prudential risks, whereas resolution actions are carried out by the Bank.
n.4: The FSCS compensates eligible claimants, not execute resolution strategies.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which global organisation coordinates anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing standards?
o: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) sets international standards to combat money laundering and terrorist financing.

n.1: The Basel Committee issues banking capital standards, not AML.
n.2: The IMF promotes global stability, not AML standards.
n.3: The World Bank funds development projects, not AML rules.
n.4: The OECD supports economic policy but FATF leads AML.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body investigates complaints about occupational pension scheme administration?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Pensions Ombudsman resolves complaints about the way occupational pension schemes are administered and disputes with trustees.

n.1: The FOS resolves consumer disputes in financial services, not occupational pensions.
n.2: The Pensions Regulator supervises governance but does not handle complaints.
n.3: The FRC regulates corporate reporting, not pensions complaints.
n.4: The PRA supervises prudential safety, not pension administration.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulator oversees advertising standards for financial promotions in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Advertising Standards Authority regulates the content of advertisements, including financial promotions, ensuring they are not misleading, harmful, or offensive.

n.1: The FCA regulates financial conduct but works alongside the ASA on advertising standards.
n.2: The PRA supervises prudential risks, not advertising.
n.3: The Bank of England manages monetary stability, not advertising.
n.4: The CMA enforces competition law, not advertising content.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which committee within the Bank of England is responsible for prudential regulation policy?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Prudential Regulation Committee oversees the PRA’s prudential regulation policy, ensuring banks and insurers are safe and sound.

n.1: The FPC addresses systemic risks, not firm-level prudential policy.
n.2: The MPC manages inflation and interest rates, not prudential regulation.
n.3: The Court is the Bank’s governing board, not its prudential policymaker.
n.4: The Audit and Risk Committee oversees internal governance, not prudential policy.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulation introduced transparency rules for EU short-selling activities?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The EU Short Selling Regulation introduced transparency and restrictions on uncovered short-selling to improve market integrity.

n.1: MiFID II covers conduct rules, not specific short-selling transparency.
n.2: UCITS governs collective investment schemes, not short-selling.
n.3: Solvency II applies to insurers, not short-selling.
n.4: PSD2 regulates payments, not short-selling.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which institution manages the UK’s Debt Management Office (DMO)?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Debt Management Office is an executive agency of HM Treasury, responsible for managing government debt issuance and cash needs.

n.1: The FCA regulates markets but does not manage government debt.
n.2: The Bank of England acts as the government’s banker, but the DMO is under Treasury.
n.3: The PRA supervises prudential risks, not government debt issuance.
n.4: The FPC oversees systemic risk, not debt management.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Who investigates breaches of the UK Corporate Governance Code?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Reporting Council investigates compliance with the UK Corporate Governance Code, focusing on accountability and transparency of listed firms.

n.1: The FCA enforces market conduct, not governance codes.
n.2: The Bank manages stability, not governance compliance.
n.3: The PRA oversees prudential risk, not governance codes.
n.4: HM Treasury sets frameworks but does not enforce governance.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK Act provides the main statutory framework for financial services regulation?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (FSMA) establishes the statutory basis for financial services regulation in the UK, underpinning the powers of the FCA and PRA.

n.1: The Banking Act 2009 introduced resolution powers, but FSMA provides the main framework.
n.2: The Companies Act governs company law, not financial services regulation.
n.3: The Enterprise Act focuses on competition and insolvency, not the main regulatory framework.
n.4: The Bribery Act covers corruption, not financial services regulation.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which regulator enforces the UK anti-money laundering regime for accountancy firms?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: HMRC supervises certain sectors, including accountancy service providers, for compliance with the UK anti-money laundering regime.

n.0: The FRC sets standards for reporting and audit, not AML enforcement.
n.1: The FCA regulates financial firms but not accountancy AML compliance.
n.3: The Bank oversees systemic stability, not AML supervision of accountancy.
n.4: The CMA enforces competition law, not AML compliance.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body provides redress for consumers in disputes with financial advisers?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Ombudsman Service provides impartial redress for disputes between financial advisers and consumers, avoiding court processes.

n.1: The Pensions Ombudsman handles occupational pension complaints, not adviser disputes.
n.2: The FCA regulates adviser conduct but does not provide dispute resolution.
n.3: The PRA ensures prudential soundness, not adviser disputes.
n.4: The Bank focuses on systemic stability, not disputes with advisers.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: What action may HM Treasury take in relation to regulators to protect public funds?
o: Issue directions on use of resolution tools involving public money
Direct the FCA to impose immediate fines on misconduct
Appoint new senior managers within firms
Mandate the PRA to waive capital requirements
Suspend the operations of the FSCS
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: HM Treasury has powers to direct regulators, particularly the Bank, where the use of public funds is involved in resolution or support measures.

n.1: Enforcement fines remain the FCA’s responsibility, not subject to Treasury directions.
n.2: Appointments within firms are regulated by SMCR, not Treasury powers.
n.3: Capital requirements are prudential rules set by regulators, not directly waived by Treasury.
n.4: FSCS operation is statutory; Treasury cannot suspend it arbitrarily.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Who oversees the UK’s Insolvency Practitioners?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Insolvency Service oversees insolvency practitioners and director disqualifications, ensuring the proper operation of the insolvency regime.

n.1: The FCA regulates conduct, not insolvency practitioners.
n.2: The Bank manages systemic stability, not insolvency practitioners.
n.3: The FRC sets audit standards, not insolvency rules.
n.4: The PRA regulates prudential risks, not insolvency professionals.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Who monitors insider dealing outside FCA enforcement powers?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Serious Fraud Office investigates and prosecutes serious or complex fraud and insider dealing cases beyond routine FCA enforcement.

n.1: The FRC oversees reporting and auditing, not insider dealing prosecutions.
n.2: The Bank focuses on systemic risks, not insider dealing.
n.3: The PRA supervises prudential risks, not criminal fraud.
n.4: The CMA deals with competition issues, not insider dealing.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which FCA tool allows it to stop misleading financial promotions immediately?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The FCA can use temporary product intervention powers to ban or restrict promotions and products that risk consumer detriment.

n.1: The countercyclical buffer is a macroprudential tool set by the FPC, not an FCA tool.
n.2: A Section 166 review assesses specific areas of a firm, not promotions.
n.3: Resolution powers are executed by the Bank of England, not the FCA.
n.4: Liquidity support is provided by the Bank of England, not the FCA.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which UK body enforces criminal law against serious market fraud?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Serious Fraud Office investigates and prosecutes serious or complex fraud and corruption, including certain cases of market-related fraud.

n.1: The FCA enforces civil and regulatory sanctions but not serious criminal fraud.
n.2: The PRA focuses on prudential regulation, not fraud prosecution.
n.3: The FRC oversees corporate reporting and audit standards, not criminal fraud.
n.4: The Bank of England manages financial stability, not prosecutions.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which Bank of England function supports market stability during liquidity shortages?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Bank of England acts as lender of last resort, providing liquidity support to solvent firms to maintain market stability.

n.1: Skilled person reviews are supervisory tools, not liquidity support.
n.2: Redress schemes are FCA tools, not Bank operations.
n.3: Listing waivers are FCA’s function, not Bank liquidity support.
n.4: Competition remedies are CMA’s role, not Bank liquidity operations.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which body regulates the professional conduct of actuaries in the UK?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Institute and Faculty of Actuaries regulates actuaries’ professional conduct, education, and ethics in the UK.

n.1: The FRC sets standards for reporting and audit but does not regulate actuaries directly.
n.2: The FCA regulates conduct of financial firms, not actuaries.
n.3: The PRA supervises prudential firms, not individual professionals.
n.4: HM Treasury sets legislation but does not regulate professional conduct.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Who sets the UK countercyclical capital buffer?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Policy Committee sets the countercyclical capital buffer to address system-wide risk.

n.1: The PRA supervises firms’ safety and soundness, whereas the macro buffer is set by the FPC.
n.2: The MPC sets interest rates for inflation control, while the FPC sets macroprudential buffers.
n.3: HM Treasury sets policy direction, but the FPC makes macroprudential buffer decisions.
n.4: The FCA focuses on conduct and markets integrity, not macroprudential capital buffers set by the FPC.

The Regulation of Financial Services.q: Which Bank of England committee is responsible for identifying systemic risks and taking macroprudential action?
The Regulation of Financial Services.w: The Financial Policy Committee is tasked with identifying systemic risks and implementing macroprudential policies to safeguard financial stability.

n.1: The PRC manages prudential supervision of firms, not systemic risk oversight.
