n.2: The MLR 2017 are compliance regulations, not the main terrorism financing statute.
n.3: The Bribery Act targets corruption offences, not terrorism financing.
n.4: The Companies Act governs corporate law, not terrorism financing.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Under POCA, what does ‘criminal property’ mean?
o: Property that constitutes a person’s benefit from criminal conduct
Assets seized by police regardless of source
Any property owned by an overseas resident
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: POCA defines criminal property as property that constitutes a person’s benefit from criminal conduct, including money or assets derived from crime.

n.1: Police seizures may involve legitimate property; criminal property must derive from crime.
n.2: Residency status does not determine whether property is criminal.
n.3: Political donations are not automatically criminal property.
n.4: Mortgage default is a civil matter, not necessarily criminal property.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which FCA Principle obliges firms to observe proper standards of market conduct?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Principle 5 requires firms to observe proper standards of market conduct in all their dealings.

n.1: Principle 2 relates to skill, care and diligence, not market conduct.
n.2: Principle 6 concerns treating customers fairly, not market conduct.
n.3: Principle 7 covers client communications, not market conduct.
n.4: Principle 9 relates to customers in relationships of trust, not conduct.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which duty is placed on firms under the Terrorism Act 2000?
o: To report knowledge or suspicion of terrorist financing
To disclose all client communications to regulators
To publish annual AML policy summaries
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: The Terrorism Act 2000 requires reporting of knowledge or suspicion of terrorist financing, similar to obligations under POCA for money laundering.

n.1: Tax reporting is not covered by the Terrorism Act.
n.2: General client communications do not require disclosure under this Act.
n.3: Audit records are separate obligations under company law, not the Terrorism Act.
n.4: Annual AML summaries are not mandated under this Act.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which is an example of enhanced due diligence under AML regulations?
o: Obtaining senior management approval for a high-risk relationship
Offering simplified disclosures to retail clients
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Enhanced due diligence may include obtaining senior management approval before establishing or continuing a relationship with a high-risk customer such as a PEP.

n.1: Staff performance reviews are HR processes, not AML EDD.
n.2: Marketing preferences are unrelated to AML.
n.3: Investment thresholds are commercial, not AML-related.
n.4: Simplified disclosures concern conduct, not AML due diligence.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: What is the main purpose of the FSCS?
o: To compensate customers if authorised firms fail
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: The FSCS provides compensation to eligible customers when authorised firms are unable to meet claims, thereby maintaining consumer confidence.

n.1: Financial crime investigations are handled by enforcement agencies, not FSCS.
n.2: Monetary policy is handled by the Bank of England, not FSCS.
n.3: Prosecutions for insider dealing fall under the FCA or SFO, not FSCS.
n.4: Financial promotions are regulated by the FCA, not FSCS.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which FCA Principle requires a firm to deal with regulators in an open and cooperative way?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Principle 11 requires firms to deal with regulators in an open and cooperative way and to disclose anything regulators would reasonably expect notice of.

n.1: Principle 4 is about financial prudence, not cooperation with regulators.
n.2: Principle 6 relates to treating customers fairly, not regulatory cooperation.
n.3: Principle 8 concerns conflicts of interest, not openness with regulators.
n.4: Principle 10 is about client asset protection, not regulatory openness.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which disputes can the Financial Ombudsman Service consider?
o: Complaints from eligible complainants against authorised firms
Disputes heard by the Competition Appeal Tribunal
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: The FOS considers complaints from eligible complainants (usually consumers and small businesses) against authorised financial firms.

n.1: General commercial disputes between companies fall outside the FOS remit.
n.2: Shareholder disputes are corporate matters, not for the FOS.
n.3: Employment disputes go to employment tribunals, not the FOS.
n.4: The Competition Appeal Tribunal handles competition law, not consumer complaints.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which dispute resolution body hears appeals against decisions made by the FCA?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: The Upper Tribunal (Tax and Chancery Chamber) hears references and appeals against certain decisions made by the FCA or PRA.

n.1: The FOS handles consumer complaints, not regulatory appeals.
n.2: High Court litigation is separate; appeals go to the Upper Tribunal first.
n.3: The FSCS provides compensation, not appeal hearings.
n.4: The CMA deals with competition, not regulatory appeals.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which data protection principle requires personal data to be kept no longer than necessary?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: The storage limitation principle requires firms to retain personal data only as long as necessary for the purposes for which it was collected.

n.1: Accuracy concerns correctness, not retention.
n.2: Purpose limitation defines use of data, not retention length.
n.3: Data minimisation governs collection, not retention.
n.4: Integrity and confidentiality relate to security, not retention.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which statutory fund protects members if a defined benefit pension scheme employer becomes insolvent?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: The Pension Protection Fund provides compensation to members of defined benefit pension schemes if the sponsoring employer becomes insolvent.

n.1: The FSCS does not cover occupational pension scheme insolvency.
n.2: The FOS resolves consumer complaints, not insolvency protection.
n.3: The Upper Tribunal is an appeals body, not a compensation fund.
n.4: The CAT handles competition law, not pensions.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: What is ‘placement’ in the context of money laundering?
o: The introduction of illicit funds into the financial system
The mixing of legitimate and illicit funds
The return of laundered money into the economy
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Placement is the first stage of money laundering, where illicit cash is first introduced into the legitimate financial system.

n.1: Layering is the second stage, involving complex transactions.
n.2: Commingling refers to mixing funds, not initial placement.
n.3: Integration is the final stage, not placement.
n.4: Concealment of beneficial ownership may occur, but it is not specifically the placement stage.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: How should a firm notify the FCA of a major systems outage impacting clients?
o: Submit a SUP 15 notification without delay
Report only in the next regulatory return
Issue a press release within 24 hours
Write to the Upper Tribunal clerk
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Firms must notify the FCA without delay under SUP 15 when significant events materially affect customers or the firm.

n.1: Waiting for periodic returns delays notification, whereas SUP 15 requires prompt reporting.
n.2: The PRA portal is irrelevant for FCA conduct notifications, while SUP 15 governs FCA reporting.
n.3: Press releases do not satisfy regulatory notification, whereas SUP 15 requires prompt FCA contact.
n.4: The Upper Tribunal handles appeals, not incident notifications required by SUP 15.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which regulator’s remit includes supervising building societies and insurers?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: The PRA is responsible for the prudential regulation and supervision of banks, building societies, credit unions, insurers and major investment firms.

n.1: The FCA regulates conduct, not prudential supervision of insurers and building societies.
n.2: The FOS resolves disputes, not prudential supervision.
n.3: The CMA focuses on competition law, not prudential oversight.
n.4: The ICO regulates data protection, not financial prudential standards.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: What is a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) submitted to?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: SARs are submitted to the UK’s National Crime Agency (NCA), which is responsible for receiving and analysing them.

n.1: The FCA supervises conduct, but SARs go to the NCA.
n.2: HM Treasury sets policy, but SARs are not filed there.
n.3: The Bank of England oversees monetary policy, not SAR submissions.
n.4: The SFO prosecutes fraud, but SARs go to the NCA.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: What is the main purpose of the FCA’s Principle 11?
o: To mandate disclosure of annual reports to clients
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Principle 11 requires a firm to deal with its regulators in an open and cooperative way and to disclose any matter of which the regulator would reasonably expect notice.

n.1: Annual reports to clients are not specified by Principle 11.
n.2: Capital adequacy is covered under prudential rules, not Principle 11.
n.3: Pricing fairness is assessed under Consumer Duty and Principle 6, not Principle 11.
n.4: Client asset protection is Principle 10, not Principle 11.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which time limit generally applies for consumers to complain to a firm about a financial product or service?
o: Six years from the event or three years from awareness
Five years from the event regardless of awareness
Ten years from awareness of the issue
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Under DISP, consumers usually have six years from the event or three years from becoming aware of the issue to make a complaint to a firm.

n.1: Two years is shorter than the DISP rule allows.
n.2: Twelve months is incorrect; the limit is longer.
n.3: Five years is not the statutory timeframe; six or three years applies.
n.4: Ten years from awareness exceeds the permitted time.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which organisation provides consumers with an independent service for settling complaints against financial firms?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: The Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS) is the statutory body providing consumers with a free and independent means of resolving disputes with regulated financial firms.

n.1: The FCA regulates conduct but does not resolve individual complaints.
n.2: The PRA oversees prudential standards, not consumer disputes.
n.3: The CMA deals with competition issues, not individual consumer complaints.
n.4: The Upper Tribunal hears appeals against regulators, not consumer complaints.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: What is the maximum fine for breaching UK financial sanctions?
o: Up to £1 million or 50% of the value of the breach
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: OFSI can impose civil monetary penalties of up to £1 million or 50% of the value of the breach, whichever is higher.

n.1: £10,000 is too low and not aligned with OFSI powers.
n.2: £100,000 understates the statutory maximum.
n.3: £500,000 is lower than OFSI’s statutory limits.
n.4: Criminal courts may impose unlimited fines, but OFSI powers are capped as stated.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which body oversees the overall effectiveness of the FSCS?
o: Financial Conduct Authority and Prudential Regulation Authority
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Both the FCA and PRA oversee the FSCS, ensuring it fulfils its statutory role in protecting consumers and maintaining confidence in financial services.

n.1: The FOS resolves disputes but does not oversee FSCS operations.
n.2: The NCA focuses on crime and intelligence, not FSCS oversight.
n.3: The ICO supervises data protection, not FSCS.
n.4: The Competition Appeal Tribunal handles competition law, not FSCS oversight.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which is an example of a complaint eligible under the FOS jurisdiction?
o: Alleged mis-selling of a personal pension
Dispute between directors of a company
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: The FOS can hear cases of alleged mis-selling of regulated products like personal pensions brought by eligible complainants.

n.1: Director disputes are company law matters, not FOS jurisdiction.
n.2: Employment tribunals handle dismissal cases, not the FOS.
n.3: Tax disputes go to HMRC and tax tribunals, not the FOS.
n.4: Competition issues are handled by the CMA, not FOS.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which types of financial services firms can be subject to FOS complaints?
o: All FCA-authorised firms carrying on regulated activities
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Any FCA-authorised firm carrying out regulated activities can be subject to complaints through the Financial Ombudsman Service.

n.1: Banks and insurers are included, but so are many other types of firms.
n.2: Investment firms are included, but not exclusively.
n.3: Mortgage lenders are included, but so are other regulated firms.
n.4: Consumer credit providers are covered, but they are not the only category.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: What is the FCA’s Principle 6 mainly concerned with?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Principle 6 requires firms to pay due regard to customers’ interests and to treat them fairly throughout their relationship with the firm.

n.1: Market integrity is addressed under Principle 5, not Principle 6.
n.2: Disclosures relate more to Principle 7 on communications rather than Principle 6.
n.3: Client asset protection is governed by CASS rules, not directly Principle 6.
n.4: Conflicts of interest are covered by Principle 8, not Principle 6.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: What is the maximum monetary award the Financial Ombudsman Service can order a firm to pay for acts after April 2019?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: For complaints referred to FOS about acts or omissions on or after 1 April 2019, the maximum award is £350,000 plus interest and costs.

n.1: £150,000 was the former limit before April 2019.
n.2: £250,000 does not reflect the correct current statutory maximum.
n.3: £500,000 exceeds the statutory award limit.
n.4: FOS awards are capped; they are not unlimited.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which regulator focuses on conduct regulation for financial markets and firms?
o: Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: The FCA regulates conduct of business, ensuring markets work well and consumers are protected.

n.1: The PRA focuses on prudential regulation, not conduct.
n.2: The MPC sets monetary policy, not conduct regulation.
n.3: The CMA handles competition law, not financial conduct.
n.4: The FOS resolves disputes, not conduct regulation.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which lawful basis under UK GDPR allows processing of personal data to comply with AML obligations?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: AML rules are statutory; processing personal data to comply with these is lawful under the ‘legal obligation’ basis in UK GDPR.

n.1: Contractual necessity applies to fulfilling contracts, not AML compliance.
n.2: Consent is not required where there is a legal obligation to process data.
n.3: Legitimate interests are secondary; AML requires legal obligation.
n.4: Vital interests relate to protecting life, not AML compliance.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule emphasises prudence in the conduct of business?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: PRA Fundamental Rule 6 requires firms to conduct their business prudently, ensuring long-term soundness and stability.

n.1: Rule 1 is about integrity, not prudence.
n.2: Rule 2 requires skill, care and diligence, not prudence.
n.3: Rule 4 relates to financial resources, not prudence.
n.4: Rule 7 requires openness with regulators, not prudence.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which organisation funds the Financial Ombudsman Service?
o: Levy and case fees paid by regulated firms
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: The FOS is funded through a combination of levies on regulated firms and case fees charged when complaints are considered.

n.1: Consumers do not directly pay for FOS operations.
n.2: The FOS is industry-funded, not funded from general taxation.
n.3: Trade bodies do not provide voluntary funding; the levy is mandatory.
n.4: Court fines are not used to fund the FOS.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: What is the FSCS compensation limit for claims relating to insurance distribution?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: For insurance distribution business, FSCS compensation is available up to £85,000 per eligible claimant per firm.

n.1: £50,000 is outdated; the current limit is £85,000.
n.2: Unlimited cover applies only to compulsory insurance claims, not distribution.
n.3: £25,000 is incorrect; the current limit is higher.
n.4: 90% cover is used in some insurance contexts, but FSCS distribution is capped at £85,000.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which of the following best demonstrates compliance with FCA Principle 3?
o: A firm implements effective systems and controls
A firm outsources all compliance checks
A firm restricts training to new staff only
A firm prioritises marketing over governance
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Principle 3 requires firms to take reasonable care to organise and control their affairs responsibly with adequate risk management systems.

n.1: Maximising profit is not the aim of Principle 3; it focuses on controls and organisation.
n.2: Outsourcing checks does not remove a firm’s responsibility for adequate systems and controls.
n.3: Training should be ongoing and broad, not restricted to new staff, to meet Principle 3.
n.4: Marketing does not replace governance; Principle 3 requires adequate systems and organisation.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Why must firms submit regulatory returns to the FCA on time?
o: To provide supervisors with information to monitor compliance
To advertise products to potential customers
To secure tax reliefs from HMRC
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Regulatory returns give the FCA essential data to monitor firms’ financial soundness and conduct compliance.

n.1: Returns are not for marketing but for supervisory oversight.
n.2: Insurance cover is unrelated to FCA returns requirements.
n.3: Tax reliefs are granted by HMRC, not the FCA.
n.4: Submitting returns does not reduce directors’ liability; it supports supervisory monitoring.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule relates to due skill, care and diligence?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: PRA Fundamental Rule 2 requires firms to conduct their business with due skill, care and diligence.

n.1: Rule 1 covers integrity, not diligence.
n.2: Rule 4 concerns capital adequacy, not diligence.
n.3: Rule 5 deals with risk strategies, not diligence.
n.4: Rule 6 concerns prudence, not diligence.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002, what is the maximum penalty for failing to report knowledge or suspicion of money laundering?
o: Five years’ imprisonment and/or a fine
One year suspension of regulatory authorisation
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Under POCA, failure to disclose knowledge or suspicion of money laundering can result in up to five years’ imprisonment, a fine, or both.

n.1: Two years is incorrect; the maximum is five years.
n.2: Although fines may be unlimited, imprisonment of up to five years is also applicable.
n.3: Community service is not the statutory penalty under POCA.
n.4: Suspension of authorisation may be regulatory action but is not the criminal penalty under POCA.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Who ensures adviser competence under the Senior Managers and Certification Regime?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Under SM&CR, a designated Senior Manager is accountable for competence and certification within their area.

n.1: Consultants advise, whereas accountability for competence rests with a Senior Manager under SM&CR.
n.2: Marketing does not own certification, while SM&CR places responsibility with Senior Management.
n.3: The MLRO focuses on AML controls, not adviser competence overseen by a Senior Manager.
n.4: Providers are external; SM&CR accountability sits with the firm’s Senior Manager.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: What compensation level does the FSCS provide for deposits in temporary high balance situations, such as house sale proceeds?
o: Up to £1 million for six months
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Temporary high balances benefit from FSCS protection up to £1 million for six months from the date the funds are credited.

n.1: £85,000 is the standard limit, but temporary balances have higher protection.
n.2: £500,000 is not the correct statutory level.
n.3: Protection is capped at £1 million, not unlimited.
n.4: £250,000 is not the statutory figure for temporary balances.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: What is the primary role of the Joint Money Laundering Steering Group (JMLSG)?
o: To provide industry guidance on complying with AML regulations
To impose fines for AML breaches
To operate the National Crime Agency
To prosecute firms for regulatory breaches
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: The JMLSG provides detailed industry guidance, endorsed by HM Treasury, to help firms interpret and comply with AML regulations.

n.1: Legislation is created by Parliament, not JMLSG.
n.2: The FCA and OFSI impose fines, not the JMLSG.
n.3: The NCA is a government body, not operated by JMLSG.
n.4: Prosecutions are led by enforcement agencies, not JMLSG.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which legislation criminalises the laundering of proceeds from all crimes, not just serious offences?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: The Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 criminalises the laundering of proceeds from any crime, not just serious offences.

n.1: The MLR 2017 impose compliance requirements but POCA creates the offences.
n.2: The Terrorism Act targets terrorist financing, not all criminal proceeds.
n.3: The Bribery Act deals with bribery offences, not money laundering generally.
n.4: The Financial Services Act focuses on regulatory structure, not criminalising laundering.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which type of client is excluded from bringing a complaint to the FOS?
o: Large businesses with over 50 employees and turnover above £6.5m
Retail clients investing in personal pensions
Sole traders using retail investment products
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Large businesses above the FOS eligibility thresholds cannot bring complaints; FOS is designed for consumers and small entities.

n.1: Retail clients with pensions are eligible complainants.
n.2: Small charities are eligible if they fall under income thresholds.
n.3: Sole traders are eligible as individuals using financial services.
n.4: Micro-enterprises are within the scope of FOS eligibility.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: What is the FSCS protection limit for deposits held in joint accounts?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Each account holder has £85,000 FSCS protection, so a joint account with two individuals benefits from £170,000 of total protection.

n.1: £85,000 applies per person, not per joint account total.
n.2: £100,000 split is not the statutory rule; £85,000 applies per holder.
n.3: £50,000 is below the correct protection level.
n.4: £25,000 each understates the FSCS limit.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: What is the FSCS compensation limit for general insurance advice claims?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: For general insurance advice and arranging, FSCS compensation is capped at £85,000 per eligible claimant per firm.

n.1: £50,000 was the old limit, no longer applicable.
n.2: 90% cover applies to certain non-compulsory insurance, not advice claims.
n.3: £25,000 is not the statutory cap.
n.4: Cover is capped; it is not unlimited.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Under SM&CR, what is the main purpose of the firm’s Responsibility Map?
o: To set out how responsibilities are allocated across Senior Managers
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: The Responsibility Map shows how key functions and responsibilities are distributed across Senior Managers in the firm.

n.1: Customer categorisation is a COBS requirement, not part of a Responsibility Map.
n.2: Pricing structures are not recorded in the Responsibility Map.
n.3: Staff holiday entitlements are HR matters, not SM&CR accountability records.
n.4: Financial promotions approvals are separate compliance records, not part of the Responsibility Map.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which class of firms is required to contribute levies to the FSCS?
o: All authorised firms within funding classes
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: All authorised firms contribute to FSCS funding through levies allocated to their specific class, such as deposits, insurance, or investments.

n.1: Retail banks contribute but they are not the only firms subject to levies.
n.2: Insurers contribute, but FSCS levies apply across classes.
n.3: Investment firms contribute, but not exclusively.
n.4: Building societies also contribute, but they are not alone.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which type of customer is subject to enhanced due diligence under AML rules?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Enhanced due diligence must be applied to politically exposed persons due to their higher risk of involvement in corruption and money laundering.

n.1: Retail investors are subject to standard due diligence, not enhanced by default.
n.2: Corporate clients may require CDD but only high-risk ones trigger enhanced due diligence.
n.3: Employees of firms are not automatically subject to enhanced due diligence.
n.4: Mortgage applicants undergo normal checks, not enhanced unless risk factors exist.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which FCA Principle underpins the need for firms to consider customers’ information needs?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Principle 7 requires firms to pay due regard to clients’ information needs and communicate information clearly and fairly.

n.1: Principle 3 addresses risk management, not client information needs.
n.2: Principle 6 is about fair treatment, not directly communication clarity.
n.3: Principle 9 relates to trust, not communications.
n.4: Principle 10 is about client asset protection, not communications.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Under the Money Laundering Regulations 2017, which approach must firms adopt for customer due diligence?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Firms must apply a risk-based approach to customer due diligence, tailoring checks according to the risk of money laundering or terrorist financing posed by the client or transaction.

n.1: A single standardised approach ignores client-specific risks; AML requires risk-based assessments.
n.2: Minimum standards alone are insufficient; firms must adjust based on risk.
n.3: Checklists help, but AML requires more flexibility than regulator-prescribed forms.
n.4: Random monitoring is not compliant; firms must assess risk systematically.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: What is the maximum prison sentence for the principal money laundering offences under POCA?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: The principal money laundering offences under POCA carry a maximum penalty of 14 years’ imprisonment and/or an unlimited fine.

n.1: Five years applies to some failure-to-disclose offences, not the main laundering offences.
n.2: Seven years is incorrect; the maximum is 14 years.
n.3: Ten years is too low; the maximum is 14 years.
n.4: Two years is too low; this applies to tipping off, not the main offences.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which type of data is classified as ‘special category’ under UK GDPR?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Special category data includes sensitive personal data such as health information, racial or ethnic origin, and biometric data requiring extra protection.

n.1: Addresses are personal data but not special category data.
n.2: Telephone numbers are personal but not special category.
n.3: Account balances are financial but not special category.
n.4: Identification numbers are personal but not special category.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Why does the FCA enforce systems and controls requirements on authorised firms?
o: To reduce the risk of misconduct and protect consumers
To guarantee higher dividends for shareholders
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Systems and controls requirements help reduce risks of misconduct, financial crime, and mismanagement, thereby protecting consumers and markets.

n.1: Profitability is not the regulator’s objective; the focus is risk mitigation.
n.2: Marketing strategies are not addressed in SYSC systems and controls rules.
n.3: Insurance premiums are not a regulatory purpose of systems and controls.
n.4: Dividends are not guaranteed or part of FCA rules.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: How are the Financial Ombudsman Service’s decisions enforced if a firm does not comply?
o: They are binding on firms and enforceable in court
They are voluntary and have no legal standing
They require Parliamentary approval before enforcement
They are referred automatically to the PRA
They can only be pursued through the ICO
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: FOS decisions are binding on firms once accepted by the complainant and can be enforced through the courts if the firm fails to comply.

n.1: They are not voluntary; they carry legal force if accepted.
n.2: Parliamentary approval is not required for enforcement.
n.3: The PRA is not involved in enforcing Ombudsman decisions.
n.4: The ICO deals with data protection, not FOS enforcement.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which category of client is covered by the FSCS?
o: Eligible claimants, including most retail clients
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: FSCS protection applies to eligible claimants, primarily retail clients, but excludes certain categories such as large financial institutions.

n.1: Not all clients are covered; eligibility criteria apply.
n.2: Professional clients may not always qualify; retail clients are the focus.
n.3: Eligible counterparties are not the primary beneficiaries of FSCS protection.
n.4: Directors of firms do not automatically receive FSCS cover.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: When must firms send a ‘final response’ letter to a complainant under DISP rules?
o: Within eight weeks of receiving the complaint
Only if the complaint is unresolved after a year
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: DISP requires firms to issue a final response within eight weeks of receiving a complaint if it has not already been resolved.

n.1: One week is too short; firms have up to eight weeks.
n.2: One month is not the regulatory deadline.
n.3: Three months exceeds the permitted period.
n.4: Complaints must be addressed far sooner than one year.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which type of customer risk factor would typically trigger enhanced due diligence?
o: Retail clients with UK savings accounts
UK employees with standard payroll accounts
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Clients from high-risk third countries or non-residents in high-risk jurisdictions typically require enhanced due diligence under AML regulations.

n.1: UK retail savings clients are standard risk unless other factors apply.
n.2: UK payroll accounts are low-risk and not subject to enhanced due diligence.
n.3: Local mortgage borrowers generally do not trigger EDD without additional risk.
n.4: Loyalty cards are commercial features, not AML risk indicators.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Why must firms maintain adequate capital resources under PRA rules?
o: To ensure financial resilience and protect policyholders
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Adequate capital resources ensure a firm can withstand financial stress, meet obligations, and safeguard policyholders and markets.

n.1: Credit ratings may benefit, but capital adequacy is required primarily for resilience and policyholder protection.
n.2: FCA waivers are not the objective of PRA capital rules.
n.3: Tax benefits are incidental; the aim is resilience and customer protection.
n.4: Dividends are not the reason; maintaining capital is about prudential soundness.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: What is the minimum period for which customer due diligence records must be retained under AML rules?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Firms must retain customer due diligence and transaction records for at least five years after the end of a business relationship or transaction.

n.1: One year is insufficient; the requirement is five years.
n.2: Seven years may apply in tax, but AML rules specify five years.
n.3: Ten years exceeds the statutory minimum under AML.
n.4: Three years is too short; AML retention is at least five years.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Why does the FCA require firms to have effective whistleblowing arrangements?
o: To allow employees to raise concerns about misconduct safely
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Whistleblowing arrangements provide a safe channel for employees to raise concerns about misconduct or regulatory breaches without fear of retaliation.

n.1: Whistleblowing is not about marketing ideas.
n.2: Share price monitoring is unrelated to whistleblowing requirements.
n.3: Sales incentives are not the focus; the aim is safe reporting of misconduct.
n.4: Whistleblowing does not replace audits; it complements them.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which offence under POCA involves disguising the nature or source of criminal property?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Concealing criminal property, including disguising its source, is a money laundering offence under POCA.

n.1: Acquisition is a separate POCA offence, not concealing.
n.2: Failure to disclose relates to reporting obligations, not disguising property.
n.3: Tipping off refers to alerting suspects, not concealing property.
n.4: Negligence is not an explicit POCA offence.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Which FCA Principle is most directly linked to ensuring firms are well resourced and solvent?
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Principle 4, Financial Prudence, requires firms to maintain adequate financial resources.

n.1: Principle 6 relates to treating customers fairly, not solvency.
n.2: Principle 7 covers client communications, not solvency.
n.3: Principle 9 concerns customer relationships of trust, not financial resources.
n.4: Principle 11 addresses openness with regulators, not solvency.

Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.q: Under AML regulations, what is simplified due diligence?
o: Reduced customer checks for lower-risk situations
Complete exemption from all due diligence
Only identity checks on politically exposed persons
Replacing due diligence with marketing surveys
Checks carried out only after transactions complete
Regulatory Framework Principles & Rules.w: Simplified due diligence applies where the risk of money laundering or terrorist financing is low, allowing reduced checks while still meeting AML obligations.

n.1: There is no complete exemption; simplified means reduced, not eliminated.
n.2: PEPs require enhanced due diligence, not simplified.
n.3: Marketing surveys are unrelated to due diligence obligations.
n.4: Due diligence must be completed before or during the relationship, not afterwards.
